creatures.name: Allosaurus
creatures.notes: Pack leader inflicts Gnash: percentage health drain that ignores armour. Against 50+ point mutated, ascendant-saddled PvP tanks a bleed pack can out-damage a Rex line while costing a fraction of the imprint time.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Pack Leader (Allosaurus)
abilities.description: Highest-level Allosaurus becomes pack leader and gains/inflicts Gnash bleed.

abilities.name: Gnash (Armour-Ignoring Bleed)
abilities.description: Percentage-based health drain that ignores armour. Multiple sources refresh rather than stack in most versions — worth testing because Allosaurus + Deinonychus + Thylacoleo bleed teams are popular.

creatures.name: Ankylosaurus
creatures.notes: Metal gathering backbone with 80% metal weight reduction. The strategic angle: Anky line throughput determines how many turret towers you can build, which is a raid stat most players never connect to creature choice.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: metal weight reduction
abilities.description: Carries metal at a reduced encumbrance (~80%).

creatures.name: Araneo
creatures.notes: Web cocoon slows and blocks vision with no torpor and no resource cost. Webs combine with bleed and with dismount tools in ways that compound — nobody fields them because they look weak on a stat sheet.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Web Cocoon (Araneo)
abilities.description: Slows and blocks rider vision. Torpor-free crowd control that stacks conceptually with bleed teams.

creatures.name: Argentavis
creatures.notes: Carries creatures, halves the weight of many resources and holds a smithy. Its grab is a cheap substitute for a Karkinos when moving tames over walls, and its saddle repairs armour mid-raid.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: misc resources weight reduction
abilities.description: Carries misc resources at a reduced encumbrance (~50%).

creatures.name: Arthropluera
creatures.notes: Acid destroys armour durability and bypasses armour reduction — a direct counter to ascendant-saddle PvP tanks. Wild ones delete saddles; tamed ones are almost never brought to raids.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Corrosive Acid (Arthropluera)
abilities.description: Destroys armour durability and bypasses armour reduction. Wild Arthropluera are notorious for deleting saddles and riot gear; tamed ones are almost never used for it.

creatures.name: Astrodelphis
creatures.notes: TEK saddle provides both a shield and turret-like fire while warping. Whether its shield stacks with Yuty resistance is unknown; it is the strongest candidate for a 'shielded buffer' raid composition.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Star Trek Shield (Astrodelphis)
abilities.description: TEK saddle ability. Interaction with Yuty roar resistance is undocumented.

creatures.name: Baryonyx
creatures.notes: Tail spin stuns in water and its health regenerates from eating fish. In swamp/river base raids a Baryonyx line can permanently lock down enemy riders for almost no tame-slot cost.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Tail Spin Stun (Baryonyx)
abilities.description: Stuns in water. Also stuns fish-eating creature interactions; land performance is weaker.

creatures.name: Basilisk
creatures.notes: Buries itself and ambushes. Burrow gives near-total protection and can be used defensively to hide a raid party's damage dealers right next to a target wall.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Basilosaurus
creatures.notes: Immune to Electrophorus/Cnidaria shock — the only aquatic mount that can cross eel-infested water with a rider still in control. Also insulates the rider against temperature, enabling armour choices other mounts cannot afford.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Blubber Insulation (Basilosaurus)
abilities.description: Rider is insulated and protected from electric shocks. Historically the counter to Electrophorus and Cnidaria chains; deep dives cause pressure damage in some versions.

abilities.name: Immunity: Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus)
abilities.description: Ignores the Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus) effect.

creatures.name: Beelzebufo
creatures.notes: Torpor-inducing tongue swipes plus cementing paste farming. A swarm of frogs can knock out an entire enemy line rather than kill it — a completely different raid objective that most tribes never consider.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Blood Crystal Wyvern
creatures.notes: Drains health from targets and heals itself. Combined with a healer aura it becomes extremely hard to remove from a fight — a sustain model most air compositions lack.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Carcharodontosaurus
creatures.notes: Added to Survival Evolved late in the game's life. Bite-based buff/imprint-like mechanic and tail attack are documented by the community but exact multipliers and stack caps remain disputed — high-priority verification target.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Castoroides
creatures.notes: Wood weight reduction plus a smithy saddle. Deeply boring, deeply useful: it is the cheapest way to keep a siege line's structures and repairs flowing during a long push.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: wood weight reduction
abilities.description: Carries wood at a reduced encumbrance (~80%).

creatures.name: Chalicotherium
creatures.notes: Throws mud and rocks: ranged slow plus structure harassment from a cake-healable herbivore. A line of Chalicos behind a soak platform is a very low-cost suppression element.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Mud Sling (Chalicotherium)
abilities.description: Throws mud/rock that slows players. Extremely cheap to field and almost never used in PvP compositions.

creatures.name: Cnidaria
creatures.notes: Shock zones. Not tameable, but wild Cnidaria fields can be *used* as defensive terrain by an attacking party.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Compsognathus
creatures.notes: Damage scales with herd size and a big herd applies meaningful torpor. Almost free to produce in bulk, which makes it the extreme case of 'quantity has a quality all its own'.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Herd Courage (Compsognathus)
abilities.description: More Compys = more damage and more courage. Torpor from a large compy pack can KO an unprepared rider.

creatures.name: Daeodon
creatures.notes: Sustain engine of every serious boss comp. Untested questions: additive stacking of multiple Daeodons, food drain rate scaling with number of healed targets, and whether the aura reaches riders of large mounts.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Passive Healing Aura (Daeodon)
abilities.description: Consumes the Daeodon's food pool; a starving Daeodon stops healing. Whether multiple Daeodon auras additively stack is one of the most commonly assumed-but-unmeasured mechanics in the game.

creatures.name: Deinonychus
creatures.notes: Rake bleed stacks with itself, latches onto large targets and climbs walls. A pack of cheap Deinonychus is one of the most armour-ignoring damage sources in the game and is chronically under-used outside of Valguero.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Rake Bleed (Deinonychus)
abilities.description: Stacks with itself. Combined with armour-piercing allies this is one of the best answers to heavily-mutated, heavily-saddled PvP tanks.

creatures.name: Desmodus
creatures.notes: Sonar screech reveals hidden players — a direct counter to Rock Drake cloak and Shadowmane stealth. If verified, this reshapes stealth-raid meta on maps where Desmodus is available.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Sonar Screech (Desmodus)
abilities.description: Reveals hidden players/creatures. Whether it breaks Rock Drake cloak and Shadowmane stealth is a priority verification target.

creatures.name: Dimetrodon
creatures.notes: Its sail insulates eggs — a live incubator that removes the need for air-conditioning arrays. Directly increases breeding throughput, which is the real bottleneck on war lines.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Dimorphodon
creatures.notes: Fast, hard-hitting fliers that attack riders. A released swarm shreds exposed players while ignoring the saddle armour that protects their mounts — the anti-armour logic inverted.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Diplocaulus
creatures.notes: Provides an oxygen source for divers. Enables long underwater sabotage of water-base foundations without SCUBA gear — a niche that no combat stat sheet captures.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Dire Bear
creatures.notes: One of very few creatures with a *stacking* damage buff (honey). Pre-loading honey turns a mid-tier mount into a burst opener; the buff cap is undocumented and worth measuring.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Hyper-Metabolic Boost (Dire Bear)
abilities.description: Eating honey grants a stacking damage increase. One of the few genuinely stacking damage buffs available to a mid-tier mount.

creatures.name: Direwolf
creatures.notes: Pack buff and extreme speed with no saddle armour: high damage per tame slot, poor survivability. Correctly supported by a healer + buffer it becomes a flank element that out-trades far pricier mounts.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Pack Howl (Direwolf)
abilities.description: Alpha Direwolf buff originally applied to packmates including players; behaviour has changed across patches.

creatures.name: Doedicurus
creatures.notes: Curled mode reportedly caps incoming hit damage rather than applying a percentage — if true, curl counters rapid low-damage turrets far better than high-damage rockets. Needs direct measurement.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Curled Defence (Doedicurus)
abilities.description: Massive reduction at the cost of all mobility. Frequently reported as a hard cap on incoming damage per hit rather than a percentage.

creatures.name: Dunkleosteus
creatures.notes: Heavily armoured aquatic gatherer that harvests oil. Untested: whether its armour multiplier combines with Yuty resistance multiplicatively for an unkillable underwater spearhead.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Electrophorus
creatures.notes: Shock disables riders and builds torpor. A swarm of cheap tamed eels can neutralise an entire enemy aquatic raid party — but is completely countered by a single Basilosaurus.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus)
abilities.description: Locks riders and builds torpor. Basilosaurus-mounted players are immune — the classic aquatic counter.

creatures.name: Enforcer
creatures.notes: Teleport dash and wall-climbing plus bonus damage vs Reapers/Nameless. Because it climbs walls, an Enforcer pack is one of very few ways to attack a cliff/raised-base position without a flying mount.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Anti-Reaper Circuitry (Enforcer)
abilities.description: Enforcers deal bonus damage to Reapers and Nameless; teleport dash also repositions them mid-fight.

creatures.name: Equus
creatures.notes: Lasso drags players off tames and holds them — one of the only ways to forcibly separate a rider from a mount without killing either. Extremely cheap counter to mounted PvP lines.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Fjordhawk
creatures.notes: Recovers the player's inventory after death and marks targets. In a long raid the difference between losing and keeping your C4, ammo and armour is usually decisive, and no combat stat captures it.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Gacha
creatures.notes: Converts resources into crystals and a mated pair produces dramatically more. Economy underpins every war comp; Gacha throughput is a strategic multiplier that no combat theorycraft accounts for.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Paired Gacha Production
abilities.description: A mated Gacha pair produces far more crystals than two singles. Magnitude disputed.

creatures.name: Giganotosaurus
creatures.notes: Highest raw melee in the tameable roster but rage throws the rider and attacks allies. Raid plans must treat the Giga as an unreliable asset: pair with fear-immune, high-HP tanks and keep the healer at extreme range.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Rage (Giganotosaurus)
abilities.description: Rage throws the rider and attacks anything nearby, including allies. A raid composition built around a Giga must plan for friendly-fire.

creatures.name: Gigantopithecus
creatures.notes: Can equip a helmet for armour and throw riders across gaps. A cheap, armoured, throwing utility creature that doubles as a fibre engine for war structures.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Griffin
creatures.notes: Carries a passenger and performs a damage-scaling dive. A rear-rider gunner on a diving Griffin is an armoured, mobile fire platform that most air defences are not tuned for.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Kaprosuchus
creatures.notes: Lunges and carries players away from their group. The cheapest 'delete one enemy from the fight' tool on land.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Lunge Grab (Kaprosuchus)
abilities.description: Drags players off tames and away from their group. Excellent anti-rider extraction tool.

creatures.name: Karkinos
creatures.notes: Carries two creatures/players and can throw them. A Karkinos that throws an ally Deinonychus pack or an armed player over a wall is a bypass mechanic most tribes have never considered.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Light Pet (Bulbdog / Featherlight / Glowtail / Shinehorn)
creatures.notes: DOUBLE-EDGED: charge light suppresses Nameless transformation and strips Reaper damage reduction, but *empowers* Seekers. A shoulder pet that changes an entire raid's effective damage output in both directions depending on the enemy.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Charge Light Aura (Light Pets)
abilities.description: Radiates charge light. Required to keep Nameless from transforming, and powers Tek gear charge batteries in some modes.

creatures.name: Lightning Wyvern
creatures.notes: Chain lightning breath hits in a line and ignores some cover geometry. Breath does not consume stamina the way melee does, making it the standard sustained aerial damage dealer.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Lystrosaurus
creatures.notes: Parked Lystrosaurus passively accelerates levelling of the entire tribe, including imprinted combat lines being levelled for a raid. The cheapest force-multiplier in the game and still forgotten in most war plans.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Experience Aura (Lystrosaurus)
abilities.description: Applies to nearby players and tames while the Lystrosaurus is parked. Exact percentage varies between the classic 50% figure and post-balance reports — measure before relying on it.

creatures.name: Maewing
creatures.notes: Nurse mode auto-feeds babies and its gliding speed makes it the best logistics creature in the game. Changes the economics of raising a mutated war line more than any stat mutation does.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Nurse Mode (Maewing)
abilities.description: Automatically feeds nearby babies. Removes most hand-feeding labour from raising lines.

creatures.name: Magmasaur
creatures.notes: Lava-immune with a metal weight reduction and a searing projectile that scales with heat. Untested: whether its fire damage interacts with armour reduction the way Poison Wyvern gas does.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: metal weight reduction
abilities.description: Carries metal at a reduced encumbrance (~75%).

creatures.name: Mammoth
creatures.notes: War drums buff allies and a wood weight reduction makes it a logistics creature. Whether the drum and Yuty Courage stack is one of the top unanswered buff-compatibility questions in the platform.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: War Drums (Mammoth)
abilities.description: TLC-added ally buff. Whether it stacks multiplicatively with Yuty Courage Roar is unverified — this is a high-priority interaction test.

abilities.name: wood weight reduction
abilities.description: Carries wood at a reduced encumbrance (~75%).

creatures.name: Managarmr
creatures.notes: Frost breath slows, dash repositions. The most mobile creature in the game; the unexplored angle is using its slow as a *team* tool to let slow heavy hitters connect, rather than as a solo duelling gimmick.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Frost Breath Slow (Managarmr)
abilities.description: Slows and damages. One of the strongest kiting/area-denial tools on official-style servers.

creatures.name: Mantis
creatures.notes: Holds player weapons — pikes, swords and whips. A whip-wielding Mantis can dismount enemy riders, which turns a cheap creature into a hard counter to expensive mutated mounts.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Megachelon
creatures.notes: Creates an oxygen bubble, grows plants on its shell and takes a platform saddle: a self-sustaining mobile base that can host plant turrets and an entire support crew underwater.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Megalania
creatures.notes: Climbs walls and inflicts Rabies (health drain). A wall-climbing creature with a damage-over-time status is a base-bypass and attrition tool in one, and is almost never fielded.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Rabies (Megalania bite)
abilities.description: Health drain over time, transferred by Megalania bites including from tamed ones.

creatures.name: Megalosaurus
creatures.notes: Massively stronger at night, grabs and holds creatures (removing them from the fight entirely). A night-time raid window changes which creatures are viable — most tribes never schedule around it.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Nocturnal Boost (Megalosaurus)
abilities.description: Dramatically stronger at night, exhausted during the day. Sleep/nap state can be exploited to skip the day penalty on some maps — unverified.

creatures.name: Megatherium
creatures.notes: Bug Killer buff gives a large damage and regen boost after killing an insect. In insect-dense arenas and chitin runs it outperforms creatures with much higher base stats — a classic misunderstood-ability case.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Bug Killer Buff (Megatherium)
abilities.description: Triggered by killing an insect. Extremely strong inside Araneo/Onyc-dense arenas; whether Broodmother-adjacent spawns count varies by map and version.

creatures.name: Mek
creatures.notes: M.S.C.M siege cannon deletes structures; the shield module protects a push. Unresolved: whether creature auras (Yuty/Daeodon) affect Mek pilots or pass through the deployed shield.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Mek Shield Module (M.S.C.M.)
abilities.description: Deployable shield. Whether creature auras pass through the shield in both directions is undocumented.

creatures.name: Microraptor
creatures.notes: Leaps at riders and dismounts/stuns them. A handful of cheap Microraptors turns an enemy mounted line into a foot line, which is then shredded by their own friendly fire. Enormous leverage per tame slot.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Dismount Stun (Microraptor)
abilities.description: Leaps at riders and knocks them off/stuns them. The cheapest hard-counter to mounted players in the game.

creatures.name: Mosasaurus
creatures.notes: Aquatic apex with a platform saddle — an underwater mobile base. A Mosa carrying a Daeodon and turret generators is the naval equivalent of a Quetz command post.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Noglin
creatures.notes: Turns an enemy creature against its owner. The highest-skill raid opener in the game: converting a single enemy tank during a push effectively removes two creatures from the fight.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Neural Control (Noglin)
abilities.description: Takes over an enemy creature/player for a limited duration. Requires charge to recharge; one of the highest-skill-ceiling raid openers.

creatures.name: Otter
creatures.notes: Shoulder insulation for the rider plus silica pearl gathering. Enables heavy-armour loadouts in extreme-temperature raid windows (lava and snow maps).

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Oviraptor
creatures.notes: Increases egg laying of nearby females, which directly multiplies mutation-line throughput. In breeding-limited metas this is the highest ROI tame in existence.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Mate-Boosted Egg Production (Oviraptor)
abilities.description: Boosts egg laying of nearby tamed females. Magnitude not formally published.

creatures.name: Pachyrhinosaurus
creatures.notes: Calming pheromone suppresses wild aggro. Use cases almost nobody tests: walking a raid party through a wild-Giga corridor, taming under fire, and moving a siege line past wild Carno packs without a single distraction kill.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Calming Pheromone (Pachyrhinosaurus)
abilities.description: Reduces/drops aggression of wild creatures in radius. Heavily under-used for passive taming routes, egg farming in hostile biomes, and for moving raid parties through wild-carnivore terrain.

creatures.name: Paraceratherium
creatures.notes: A platform saddle on a herbivore that can be healed by Sweet Vegetable Cakes — a self-sustaining mobile bunker that can carry a generator, turrets and a Daeodon. Almost never used in this configuration.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Parasaurolophus
creatures.notes: Threat scan is a persistent, free radar. Parking tamed Parasaur sentries around a base or along a raid approach line gives early warning that costs almost nothing to maintain.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Threat Scan (Parasaurolophus)
abilities.description: Pings hostile creatures/players. Cheap, underrated raid-screening tool.

creatures.name: Phoenix
creatures.notes: Fire tornado damages structures and creatures while it harvests. Its heat aura and fiery claw mean it is both a siege tool and a smelter — the rarest multi-role raider in the game.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Poison Wyvern
creatures.notes: Cloud damage is reported to ignore armour and hit the rider directly — so a Poison Wyvern is a counter to *saddle-armour-stacked* tanks, not to HP. Countered by hazard suits, which are almost never pre-positioned.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Poison Cloud (Poison Wyvern)
abilities.description: Cloud damage is widely reported to ignore armour and hit the rider directly. Countered by hazard suits/gas masks rather than armour values.

creatures.name: Procoptodon
creatures.notes: Carries a player in its pouch across huge distances in a single jump chain. A pouched player with C4 or a Noglin is a delivery mechanism most defences are not built for.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Pulmonoscorpius
creatures.notes: Stacks torpor without damaging targets — the tool for capturing enemy tames alive rather than destroying them, which is a raid outcome with far higher payoff than a kill.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Purlovia
creatures.notes: Buries itself and its rider, including as a hidden storage vault. Off-map caches of Purlovia with backup gear change raid economics, and buried ambushers are nearly impossible to pre-clear.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Quetzal
creatures.notes: Flying platform. The under-used angle is an aerial command post: a Quetz carrying a Daeodon + Yuty pair that keeps buffs/healing airborne over a ground push.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Raptor
creatures.notes: Pack buff and pounce. Cheapest mass-producible pack unit — the interesting research question is whether a buffed raptor pack beats an unbudgeted Rex line per unit of breeding time.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Pack Buff (Raptor)
abilities.description: Alpha-led raptor packs gain a damage bonus and a roar that briefly scares smaller creatures.

creatures.name: Reaper King
creatures.notes: High innate damage reduction — unless charge light is present, which strips most of it. Most players learn this as a defensive fact about enemies and never weaponise it against enemy Reaper lines.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Immunity: Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus)
abilities.description: Ignores the Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus) effect.

abilities.name: Immunity: Blubber Insulation (Basilosaurus)
abilities.description: Ignores the Blubber Insulation (Basilosaurus) effect.

creatures.name: Rex
creatures.notes: Benchmark for every other damage creature. High saddle armour cap makes it the default boss front-liner, but it has zero utility and no rider protection — it is often outperformed per-point-invested by buffed mid-tier creatures.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Rock Drake
creatures.notes: Cloaks rider and mount, glides, and is radiation-immune — the only large mount that can operate in entire zones other creatures cannot enter. Cloak + radiation immunity creates raid routes no other composition can attempt.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Cloaking (Rock Drake)
abilities.description: Cloaks rider and mount. Does not hide footprints, sound, or Nameless aggro.

creatures.name: Rock Elemental
creatures.notes: Bullets do essentially nothing. The standard answer to a heavy turret wall is a Rock Elemental leading the push while the actual damage dealers follow behind it. Takes real damage from explosives and creature melee only.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Mineralised Hide (Rock Elemental)
abilities.description: Projectiles deal almost nothing; explosives and creature melee still work. This is the single most important turret-soak rule in raid planning.

creatures.name: Sarco
creatures.notes: Cheap, fast in water, with a grab-lunge that drags players under. The cheapest aquatic rider-removal tool and the base of any budget water-raid composition.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Shadowmane
creatures.notes: Group stealth plus a warp-stun and a self/pack heal. Almost certainly the strongest 'does everything' creature for organised tribes, and the most common source of undocumented interaction reports.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Shadowmane Group Stealth
abilities.description: Conceals nearby allies from wild creatures. Interaction with Desmodus sonar is untested.

creatures.name: Sinomacrops
creatures.notes: Glider + parachute ability for the rider, plus weight reduction on the player's inventory. Turns any rider into a gliding insertion unit — an infiltration vector most defences ignore entirely.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Snow Owl
creatures.notes: The only flying healer. Frozen Vision both heals allies and freezes enemies; owl vision detects players through cover. Under-explored: freeze-cycling enemy front-liners while simultaneously topping up your own tank line.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Frozen Vision Heal (Snow Owl)
abilities.description: Allies encased in ice are healed but also immobilised and briefly vulnerable. The same ability freezes enemies — a double-edged tool in mixed melee fights.

creatures.name: Spinosaurus
creatures.notes: Hydration buff + four-legged stance turn-rate is a genuinely different damage profile to Rex in water arenas and swamp raids. Almost never theorycrafted for water-boss or river-base raids.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Hydration Buff (Spinosaurus)
abilities.description: Applies while touching water; the four-legged stance also changes turn radius and hitbox.

creatures.name: Stegosaurus
creatures.notes: Hardened plates protect the rider, turning a Stego into a mobile bunker for a rider who must stay mounted (e.g. a Noglin operator or a rocket-wielding gunner). Combined with cake healing this is a very cheap soak platform.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Hardened Plate Mode (Stegosaurus)
abilities.description: Hardened plates protect the rider from a large share of damage. Combined with a rider dismount-immunity effect this becomes a mobile bunker.

creatures.name: Tapejara
creatures.notes: Two independent rider seats and the ability to hover while facing any direction — a flying gun platform and, more importantly, a flying *command post* for a raid leader directing buffs.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: TEK Stryder
creatures.notes: Carries enormous weight and can teleport with a linked tribe network. Strategic rather than tactical: it changes how fast a war line can be re-supplied and re-positioned mid-campaign.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Therizinosaurus
creatures.notes: A herbivore with carnivore-tier melee that can be healed by Sweet Vegetable Cakes. On paper a cake-healed, buffed Theri line is one of the most efficient front lines in the game and is rarely used that way.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Thylacoleo
creatures.notes: Pounce pins players and ignores part of armour; tree-ambush positioning makes it a mobile anti-rider picket. Often skipped because players over-value Rex-line HP in open-field fights.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Pounce Pin (Thylacoleo)
abilities.description: Pins players and applies bleed. Pounce from trees is the classic ambush dismount tool.

creatures.name: Titanosaur
creatures.notes: Walks through structures and soaks entire turret networks, but does not feed — it dies when its food runs out. Any Titanosaur strategy must be time-boxed, which changes the entire raid plan shape.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Triceratops
creatures.notes: Rivalry triggers against large carnivores — including enemy tamed Rex/Giga lines. A cheap, cake-healable, buff-carrying counter to carnivore-heavy defence comps, almost never theorycrafted.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Rivalry (Triceratops)
abilities.description: Triggers when near a larger carnivore (Rex, Spino, Giga, Yuty). Community usually reports a damage and resistance increase; exact values and trigger radius are not formally published.

creatures.name: Tusoteuthis
creatures.notes: Grabs creatures and players (removing rider agency), blinds with ink and drains oxygen. A grab + bleed combination is effectively a guaranteed kill on any lone aquatic target.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Immunity: Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus)
abilities.description: Ignores the Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus) effect.

creatures.name: Velonasaur
creatures.notes: Turret mode turns it into a living auto-turret with no ammo cost. Combined with a Yuty roar and Daeodon sustain it is the backbone of both offline defence and boss damage, and it is still cheaper to raise than a Rex line.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Turret Mode (Velonasaur)
abilities.description: Stationary spray mode. Sustained fire drains stamina/food; the damage falloff radius is not documented.

creatures.name: Vulture
creatures.notes: Flocking damage bonus on a shoulder pet. A flock released over an enemy rider stacks damage from a direction most players never screen against, at trivial cost.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Flock (Vulture)
abilities.description: Damage increases with nearby Vultures. Shoulder-mount swarm archetype.

creatures.name: Woolly Rhino
creatures.notes: Charge attack damage scales with run-up speed. Combined with a slow on the target (Managarmr frost breath / Chalico mud) the target cannot dodge, converting a situational attack into a reliable opener.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

creatures.name: Yutyrannus
creatures.notes: The single highest-leverage support mount in the game: one roar multiplies the output of every creature in the party. Overlooked angles: (1) fear roar's own-team collateral, (2) whether two Yutys stagger roars to maintain 100% uptime without overlap, (3) roar radius vs. arena walls.

abilities.name: Bite / Melee
abilities.description: Standard melee attack; damage scales with melee stat points and saddles do not add damage.

abilities.name: Courage Roar (Yutyrannus)
abilities.description: Two Yutyrannus roars refresh the same buff rather than stacking; the buff applies to allied tames and players in radius. Exact radius differs between versions — needs measurement.

abilities.name: Fear Roar (Yutyrannus)
abilities.description: Routs wild and tamed creatures below a level threshold. CRITICAL CONFLICT: the roar is not ally-selective in many versions — your own low-level tames and shoulder pets can be routed by your own Yuty.

buffs.name: Courage Roar (Yutyrannus)
buffs.notes: Two Yutyrannus roars refresh the same buff rather than stacking; the buff applies to allied tames and players in radius. Exact radius differs between versions — needs measurement.

buffs.name: Fear Roar (Yutyrannus)
buffs.notes: Routs wild and tamed creatures below a level threshold. CRITICAL CONFLICT: the roar is not ally-selective in many versions — your own low-level tames and shoulder pets can be routed by your own Yuty.

buffs.name: Passive Healing Aura (Daeodon)
buffs.notes: Consumes the Daeodon's food pool; a starving Daeodon stops healing. Whether multiple Daeodon auras additively stack is one of the most commonly assumed-but-unmeasured mechanics in the game.

buffs.name: Frozen Vision Heal (Snow Owl)
buffs.notes: Allies encased in ice are healed but also immobilised and briefly vulnerable. The same ability freezes enemies — a double-edged tool in mixed melee fights.

buffs.name: Experience Aura (Lystrosaurus)
buffs.notes: Applies to nearby players and tames while the Lystrosaurus is parked. Exact percentage varies between the classic 50% figure and post-balance reports — measure before relying on it.

buffs.name: Mate-Boosted Egg Production (Oviraptor)
buffs.notes: Boosts egg laying of nearby tamed females. Magnitude not formally published.

buffs.name: Calming Pheromone (Pachyrhinosaurus)
buffs.notes: Reduces/drops aggression of wild creatures in radius. Heavily under-used for passive taming routes, egg farming in hostile biomes, and for moving raid parties through wild-carnivore terrain.

buffs.name: War Drums (Mammoth)
buffs.notes: TLC-added ally buff. Whether it stacks multiplicatively with Yuty Courage Roar is unverified — this is a high-priority interaction test.

buffs.name: Shadowmane Group Stealth
buffs.notes: Conceals nearby allies from wild creatures. Interaction with Desmodus sonar is untested.

buffs.name: Nurse Mode (Maewing)
buffs.notes: Automatically feeds nearby babies. Removes most hand-feeding labour from raising lines.

buffs.name: Paired Gacha Production
buffs.notes: A mated Gacha pair produces far more crystals than two singles. Magnitude disputed.

buffs.name: Star Trek Shield (Astrodelphis)
buffs.notes: TEK saddle ability. Interaction with Yuty roar resistance is undocumented.

buffs.name: Rivalry (Triceratops)
buffs.notes: Triggers when near a larger carnivore (Rex, Spino, Giga, Yuty). Community usually reports a damage and resistance increase; exact values and trigger radius are not formally published.

buffs.name: Hydration Buff (Spinosaurus)
buffs.notes: Applies while touching water; the four-legged stance also changes turn radius and hitbox.

buffs.name: Bug Killer Buff (Megatherium)
buffs.notes: Triggered by killing an insect. Extremely strong inside Araneo/Onyc-dense arenas; whether Broodmother-adjacent spawns count varies by map and version.

buffs.name: Hyper-Metabolic Boost (Dire Bear)
buffs.notes: Eating honey grants a stacking damage increase. One of the few genuinely stacking damage buffs available to a mid-tier mount.

buffs.name: Nocturnal Boost (Megalosaurus)
buffs.notes: Dramatically stronger at night, exhausted during the day. Sleep/nap state can be exploited to skip the day penalty on some maps — unverified.

buffs.name: Rage (Giganotosaurus)
buffs.notes: Rage throws the rider and attacks anything nearby, including allies. A raid composition built around a Giga must plan for friendly-fire.

buffs.name: Curled Defence (Doedicurus)
buffs.notes: Massive reduction at the cost of all mobility. Frequently reported as a hard cap on incoming damage per hit rather than a percentage.

buffs.name: Hardened Plate Mode (Stegosaurus)
buffs.notes: Hardened plates protect the rider from a large share of damage. Combined with a rider dismount-immunity effect this becomes a mobile bunker.

buffs.name: Mineralised Hide (Rock Elemental)
buffs.notes: Projectiles deal almost nothing; explosives and creature melee still work. This is the single most important turret-soak rule in raid planning.

buffs.name: Blubber Insulation (Basilosaurus)
buffs.notes: Rider is insulated and protected from electric shocks. Historically the counter to Electrophorus and Cnidaria chains; deep dives cause pressure damage in some versions.

buffs.name: Turret Mode (Velonasaur)
buffs.notes: Stationary spray mode. Sustained fire drains stamina/food; the damage falloff radius is not documented.

buffs.name: Cloaking (Rock Drake)
buffs.notes: Cloaks rider and mount. Does not hide footprints, sound, or Nameless aggro.

buffs.name: Sonar Screech (Desmodus)
buffs.notes: Reveals hidden players/creatures. Whether it breaks Rock Drake cloak and Shadowmane stealth is a priority verification target.

buffs.name: Threat Scan (Parasaurolophus)
buffs.notes: Pings hostile creatures/players. Cheap, underrated raid-screening tool.

buffs.name: Mate Boost
buffs.notes: Applies when a mated pair is nearby. Universally available and universally forgotten when players theorycraft 'optimal' comps.

buffs.name: Pack Buff (Raptor)
buffs.notes: Alpha-led raptor packs gain a damage bonus and a roar that briefly scares smaller creatures.

buffs.name: Pack Howl (Direwolf)
buffs.notes: Alpha Direwolf buff originally applied to packmates including players; behaviour has changed across patches.

buffs.name: Pack Leader (Allosaurus)
buffs.notes: Highest-level Allosaurus becomes pack leader and gains/inflicts Gnash bleed.

buffs.name: Flock (Vulture)
buffs.notes: Damage increases with nearby Vultures. Shoulder-mount swarm archetype.

buffs.name: Herd Courage (Compsognathus)
buffs.notes: More Compys = more damage and more courage. Torpor from a large compy pack can KO an unprepared rider.

buffs.name: Charge Light Aura (Light Pets)
buffs.notes: Radiates charge light. Required to keep Nameless from transforming, and powers Tek gear charge batteries in some modes.

buffs.name: Charge Light Vulnerability (Reaper)
buffs.notes: Charge light strips a large part of a Reaper's damage reduction. Counter-intuitive: a shoulder pet that seems purely cosmetic roughly doubles effective damage from your whole raid party against Reapers.

buffs.name: Charge Light Suppression (Nameless)
buffs.notes: Prevents Nameless mutating into the far more dangerous altered form.

buffs.name: Charge Empowerment (Seeker)
buffs.notes: INVERTED INTERACTION: the same charge light that cripples Reapers and Nameless *buffs* Seekers. Taking a light pet into a Seeker-infested route is actively harmful.

buffs.name: Anti-Reaper Circuitry (Enforcer)
buffs.notes: Enforcers deal bonus damage to Reapers and Nameless; teleport dash also repositions them mid-fight.

buffs.name: Gnash (Armour-Ignoring Bleed)
buffs.notes: Percentage-based health drain that ignores armour. Multiple sources refresh rather than stack in most versions — worth testing because Allosaurus + Deinonychus + Thylacoleo bleed teams are popular.

buffs.name: Rake Bleed (Deinonychus)
buffs.notes: Stacks with itself. Combined with armour-piercing allies this is one of the best answers to heavily-mutated, heavily-saddled PvP tanks.

buffs.name: Corrosive Acid (Arthropluera)
buffs.notes: Destroys armour durability and bypasses armour reduction. Wild Arthropluera are notorious for deleting saddles and riot gear; tamed ones are almost never used for it.

buffs.name: Dismount Stun (Microraptor)
buffs.notes: Leaps at riders and knocks them off/stuns them. The cheapest hard-counter to mounted players in the game.

buffs.name: Tail Spin Stun (Baryonyx)
buffs.notes: Stuns in water. Also stuns fish-eating creature interactions; land performance is weaker.

buffs.name: Bioelectric Shock (Electrophorus)
buffs.notes: Locks riders and builds torpor. Basilosaurus-mounted players are immune — the classic aquatic counter.

buffs.name: Tentacle Grab & Ink (Tusoteuthis)
buffs.notes: Holds creatures/players, drains oxygen and blinds with ink. Grabbed riders cannot use most saddles.

buffs.name: Lunge Grab (Kaprosuchus)
buffs.notes: Drags players off tames and away from their group. Excellent anti-rider extraction tool.

buffs.name: Frost Breath Slow (Managarmr)
buffs.notes: Slows and damages. One of the strongest kiting/area-denial tools on official-style servers.

buffs.name: Mud Sling (Chalicotherium)
buffs.notes: Throws mud/rock that slows players. Extremely cheap to field and almost never used in PvP compositions.

buffs.name: Web Cocoon (Araneo)
buffs.notes: Slows and blocks rider vision. Torpor-free crowd control that stacks conceptually with bleed teams.

buffs.name: Neural Control (Noglin)
buffs.notes: Takes over an enemy creature/player for a limited duration. Requires charge to recharge; one of the highest-skill-ceiling raid openers.

buffs.name: Pounce Pin (Thylacoleo)
buffs.notes: Pins players and applies bleed. Pounce from trees is the classic ambush dismount tool.

buffs.name: Poison Cloud (Poison Wyvern)
buffs.notes: Cloud damage is widely reported to ignore armour and hit the rider directly. Countered by hazard suits/gas masks rather than armour values.

buffs.name: Swamp Fever
buffs.notes: Disease from Diseased Leeches; cured with Lesser Antidote. Affects stats and food/water drain.

buffs.name: Rabies (Megalania bite)
buffs.notes: Health drain over time, transferred by Megalania bites including from tamed ones.

buffs.name: Medical Brew
buffs.notes: Player-only healing; does not heal mounts. Note the interaction with creature healing auras for rider survivability.

buffs.name: Sweet Vegetable Cake
buffs.notes: Heals herbivores only — the single most under-used raid-support item for herbivore tank lines (Turtles, Trikes, Paracers, Stegos).

buffs.name: Shadow Steak Saute
buffs.notes: Community reports a meaningful damage reduction plus hypothermal insulation. Exact reduction percentage is disputed — measure before stacking calculations.

buffs.name: Calien Soup
buffs.notes: Heat protection. Enables desert/lava-map armour choices that would otherwise be impossible.

buffs.name: Fria Curry
buffs.notes: Cold protection; snow-map offensive window enabler.

buffs.name: Hazard Suit
buffs.notes: Immune to gas-based debuffs, including several creature clouds. Low armour value — trade-off must be planned.

buffs.name: TEK Suit
buffs.notes: Flight/blink mobility. Pairs with creature auras that are normally lost when the player dismounts.

buffs.name: Mek Shield Module (M.S.C.M.)
buffs.notes: Deployable shield. Whether creature auras pass through the shield in both directions is undocumented.

bosses.name: Broodmother Lysrix
bosses.notes: Insect spawns feed Megatherium's Bug Killer buff; whether boss-adjacent spiders trigger it reliably on every map is a live verification question. Bleed is armour-independent and strong against high-HP bosses.

bosses.name: Megapithecus
bosses.notes: Minion pressure favours sustain + buffed melee. Therizinosaur lines are cake-healable, which raises effective staying power relative to cost.

bosses.name: Dragon
bosses.notes: Fire breath is percentage-based damage over time; healing throughput matters more than raw HP. Ranged damage dealers avoid the melee clump where breath lands.

bosses.name: Overseer
bosses.notes: Tek cave temperature stages make insulation support relevant — a rarely modelled constraint.

bosses.name: Rockwell
bosses.notes: Radiation gates the entire composition: only radiation-immune mounts can stay in the arena. Charge light from light pets strips Reaper damage reduction inside this fight.

bosses.name: King Titan
bosses.notes: Mek siege modules and buffed Giga lines are the documented approach; the interaction of Mek shields with creature auras is undocumented.

bosses.name: Desert Titan
bosses.notes: Flying boss makes ground-only melee compositions useless — the most common raid-planning error.

bosses.name: Master Controller (Corrupted Master Controller)
bosses.notes: Shadowmane and Astrodelphis dominate here; both have ability interactions that are not fully documented.
